actions.newValue: Built around Jim Steinman's songs for Meat Loaf's best-known album, the musical follows Strat, who is infatuated with Raven, the daughter of the sinister overlord Falco. Their romance puts the story in Romeo and Juliet territory, with the emotional volume dialled up well past eleven.
actions.description: BRO-6075: backfill empty West End historical synopsis, written from the show's collected review texts

actions.newValue: Harry and his wife Max live in a perfectly nice suburban Middle England, where their son Nick refuses to behave like the perfect boy they imagine and goes missing on a bender. They decide to buy a replacement, Jan, a teenager delivered in a flatpack and assembled on stage from an instruction manual. At first things go well, in Thomas Eccleshare's sci-fi satire.
actions.description: BRO-6075: backfill empty West End historical synopsis, written from the show's collected review texts

actions.newValue: James Graham's play tells the story of Charles Ingram, the Coughing Major, who won Who Wants to Be a Millionaire in 2001 and was then prosecuted over evidence that his wife Diana and an accomplice had coughed to signal the right answers. The audience is invited to decide whether the Ingrams were guilty or were framed by paranoid show producers.
actions.description: BRO-6075: backfill empty West End historical synopsis, written from the show's collected review texts

actions.newValue: Based on the true story of North Korean commandos abducting people from Japanese coastal towns in the autumn of 1977, the play follows two sisters, Reiko and Hanako, who are separated when Hanako is on the beach as a great wave crashes ashore and is abducted. Over the years she is indoctrinated, given a husband and has a child, while her mother and sister never lose hope and fight for recognition of her disappearance.
actions.description: BRO-6075: backfill empty West End historical synopsis, written from the show's collected review texts

actions.newValue: Dennis Kelly's monologue, performed by Carey Mulligan, has a woman recount her life in a series of conversational speeches, from the moment she spots her future husband in an airport queue. His confidence rockets her, a working-class woman with no relevant experience, into a dazzling television career, as she looks back at the ups and downs of their relationship.

actions.newValue: The writer and performer Rob Drummond plays himself and hands each audience member a keypad to vote on moral dilemmas and on the direction of the story. The evening recounts a series of encounters with a possibly delusional bee-keeping activist in the Highlands, and questions how votes influence outcomes.
actions.description: BRO-6075: backfill empty West End historical synopsis, written from the show's collected review texts

actions.newValue: In 1934, during the Great Depression, a group of wayward travellers come together at Nick Laine's run-down guesthouse in Duluth, Minnesota. Conor McPherson's play is told through the songs of Bob Dylan and places an ill-assorted group of characters together in a temporary, insecure refuge.
actions.description: BRO-6075: backfill empty West End historical synopsis, written from the show's collected review texts

actions.newValue: Helen Edmundson's play depicts the reign of Anne, the last Stuart monarch, who died in 1714. It centres on her fervid relationship with Sarah Churchill, her childhood friend and frenemy, as the friendship between the two women shapes the fate of the crown.
actions.description: BRO-6075: backfill empty West End historical synopsis, written from the show's collected review texts

actions.newValue: Kenneth Grahame's 1908 tale of Mr. Toad, Ratty and their animal friends becomes a musical at the London Palladium. The animals dance through spring and mess about in boats in this retelling of the perennially popular story.
actions.description: BRO-6075: backfill empty West End historical synopsis, written from the show's collected review texts

actions.newValue: Quinn Carney, a divided Irish hero and father of seven, presides over a crowded farmhouse full of family, in a play packed with secrets, confessions, political and sexual clashes and betrayals. Jez Butterworth's drama, directed by Sam Mendes with a cast of 21, mixes ballads, dancing and wrestling with banshee wails and a violent past.
actions.description: BRO-6075: backfill empty West End historical synopsis, written from the show's collected review texts

actions.newValue: Tom Stoppard's play is set in 1917 Zurich, where art and politics collide in a library. Henry Carr, a former consular attache with a failing memory, narrates the story, and his fallible recall jumbles the dates into a comic fantasy that takes in a Leninist lecture.
actions.description: BRO-6075: backfill empty West End historical synopsis, written from the show's collected review texts

actions.newValue: Richard and Katie's bodies collide one night after they meet in a nightclub at a hen party and stag do. Katie, still nursing a broken heart, sees a one night stand, while geeky Richard sees a future. A rhyming two-hander told in verse, the 75-minute rom-com follows them from drunken bus stop dances to stolen breakfasts.
